title: Two-asset Grove Instances need an aggregate normalized rate limit on top of per-asset limits to stop splitting from multiplying exposure
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.3 declares RateLimitIDs for "this Instance's deposit, withdrawal, and swap operations," and the subdocuments reveal a two-level structure: an **Aggregate Deposit RateLimitID** (`0xd3384d54…`) and an **Aggregate Withdrawal RateLimitID** (`0xbe8cbf4b…`) sitting above per-asset IDs for AUSD and USDC.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.4.1 then sets the aggregate deposit `maxAmount` to "5,000,000 (normalized)" while *also* setting the AUSD leg to 5,000,000 AUSD and the USDC leg to 5,000,000 USDC.

The per-asset limits alone would be unsound. A two-asset conduit lets an operator supply the full allowance in each asset, so identical 5,000,000 caps would authorize 10,000,000 of economic exposure while every individual limit remained satisfied. The aggregate limit closes that gap, and the word *normalized* is what makes it possible — the two legs must be converted to a common unit before they can be summed against one ceiling.

The pattern generalizes to any multi-asset allocation: per-asset limits bound the shape of the position, an aggregate limit bounds its size, and only the aggregate corresponds to the risk mandate. Note that the Uniswap Swaps Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.1.2.4.3) and LP Instance (.12.2.2.4.1) instead express their two-asset limits in the combined unit "AUSD/USDC" — a lighter approach that achieves the same ceiling but loses the ability to bound each leg separately.
description: The Diamond PAU Instance registers aggregate deposit and withdrawal RateLimitIDs beside AUSD and USDC ones; without the aggregate, two 5M per-asset caps would permit 10M of combined exposure.
